messages:
maya: Heads up — CI perf job failed after merging the model bump PR (rwd-3b -> rwd-3b-v2). p50 ~ same, but p95 +22% and p99 +48% on the serving perf job. Link: https://ci.redwood/internal/perf/9876 :alarm_clock:

jorge: Ugh. Any obvious error in the logs?  Did the runtime pick a different kernel or quant path?

maya: Logs show a kernel fallback during autoregressive step. Example from the trace:
```
[2026-03-17T18:07:12Z] selected_kernel: attention_opt_v2
[2026-03-17T18:07:12Z] fallback_kernel: attention_ref_fp32 (mismatch: config.dropout=false vs runtime-expected dropout flag)
[2026-03-17T18:07:12Z] kernel_latency_ms: 8.1 -> 24.7 (fallback)
```
Also tokenizer difference: new checkpoint seems to emit an extra BOS token for some inputs which increases average sequence length by ~6 tokens in our smoke prompts. That amplifies KV cache misses and changes batching behavior.

sasha: I can start a bisect. If kernel fallback is the culprit we should see the perf step change when the model metadata or kernel selector policy changed. Jorge — can you dump the model metadata used at serving time? Especially the config keys: `rotary_dim`, `use_cache`, `tokenizer_version`, `max_sequence_length` etc.

jon (perf-bot): perf-bot: Automated regression alert: perf/serving/pipeline p99 increased by 48% on 1764123000 -> 1764123400. Attached flamegraph and trace id perf-1764123456.

maya: Pushed the model metadata snapshot to the PR: https://git.internal/models/rwd-3b-v2/metadata.json
quick diff: `tokenizer_version: 2.1` (was 2.0), `use_cache: true` (same), `rotary_dim: 64` (same), `layernorm_eps` changed from 1e-5 -> 1e-6.

jorge: layernorm_eps shouldn't change kernel selection. Tokenizer bump could change tokenization boundaries (more tokens -> longer seq). But the kernel fallback log mentions a mismatch for a boolean flag — sounds like the runtime expected `dropout` flag present in model attrs. Did onboarding pipeline drop a flag?

sasha: Bisect started. Quick run shows commit 4c9b2f4 (model onboarding: strip optional metadata keys) makes perf go bad. That commit removed some metadata keys that our kernel selector relied on.

maya: Oh damn — that onboarding script was trying to canonicalize metadata and removed `kernel_hint` and `runtime_flags`. Those were optional but we implicitly used them for optimized kernels.

jorge: So the runtime falls back to generic FP32 reference kernels because the selector can't find `kernel_hint=attention_opt_v2`. That explains the ~3x kernel latency increase.

eng-runtime-oncall: Confirmed on a canary of 10 hosts: when metadata lacks `kernel_hint` we pick `attention_ref_fp32`. Heatmap attached: p99 before 12ms, after 34ms.

release-cop: This is a rollout blocker. We need either a revert of the onboarding change or an emergency fix that preserves `kernel_hint` in model metadata. What's lower risk?

sasha: Revert in model registry + re-push the previous metadata is fastest. I'll open an emergency PR to re-add the removed keys for all affected models (rwd-3b-v2 and any recent bumps).

maya: Also need to add a CI check: onboarding should fail if required kernel selector keys are missing. Right now everything passes because keys were optional.

jorge: For longer term, selector should be more defensive — fallback cost is huge. We should:
- log a hard warning and metric when `kernel_hint` missing
- add a unit test that ensures rwd models select optimized kernels
- and ensure tokenizer changes are visible in the perf smoke to catch seq length regressions

maya: Running a quick local revert of the metadata for rwd-3b-v2 now. Patch: `gsutil cp metadata.json metadata.json.bak && echo '{"kernel_hint":"attention_opt_v2","runtime_flags":{"use_fast_attention":true}}' > metadata.json && gsutil cp metadata.json gs://models/rwd-3b-v2/`

perf-bot: perf-bot: After metadata restore, perf job re-run shows p99 back down to +5% vs baseline (within noise). Regression marked resolved in the incident dashboard.

sasha: PR up: #2208 — emergency: preserve kernel selector keys during onboarding. Also added a lint rule and an integration perf check that runs a short trace to verify optimized kernel chosen (checks `selected_kernel` in the runtime trace).

release-cop: Approving rollback path. We should still run a follow-up to properly onboard tokenizer v2.1 — that extra BOS behavior needs to be characterized so batching heuristics don't oscillate.

jorge: Agreed. Action items: (1) Revert onboarding change for optional metadata (sasha) — done in PR #2208, (2) Add CI selector test (sasha), (3) Add perf test that asserts average seq len delta < 2 tokens for model bumps (maya), (4) Postmortem + blameless update to onboarding docs (maya/jorge).

maya: I'll draft the postmortem and schedule a short retro. Thanks all for the quick triage :thumbsup:

sasha: Note for follow-up — tokenizer changes should be validated with a small corpus of production prompts. I'll add that to the onboarding checklist.

eng-runtime-oncall: Marking thread resolved for now. Will keep watch for any additional regressions during the next rollout window.
